newsitem.title: USA: U S West to change Continental deal - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: U S West to change Continental deal - WSJ.

text.p: U S West Inc's U S West Media Group is considering boosting the cash portion of its $5.3 billion purchase of Continental Cablevision Inc in order to offset a 31-percent drop in the value of its stock, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
The newspaper said the company's Media Group stock had fallen since it announced plans for the acquisition last February.
U S West wanted to prevent the drop in the share price from ruining the deal, it said, adding that more cash instead of more stock would avoid a greater dilution.
The newspaper, which quoted "executives" close to the talks, said the company hoped to reach a deal with Continental to boost up to $1 billion in extra cash this week.

Under the original agreement, U S West would pay part of the acquisition in stock at $24.50 a share, it said, explaining how the part would cover between $2.8 billion and $3.3 billion of the total $5.3 billion amount.
Cash and preferred stock would cover the rest, it added.
One Friday, U S West's Media Group stock closed at $16-7/8.
